extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), USPTO OED staff, and parties/respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order resolving disciplinary action by stipulation, stating jurisdictional bases, stipulated facts, legal conclusions under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, and agreed sanctions and procedures for further discipline. Used to document required practitioner conduct, notification duties, sanctions, publication, and processes for additional suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered patent agents/attorneys must follow the Rules of Professional Conduct in all practice before the Office; violations are grounds for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26, 11.32, and 11.39.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies statutory and regulatory authority under which OED brings and the Director decides disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of conviction requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being convicted of a crime in a court of the United States, any State, or a foreign country, a practitioner subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office shall notify the OED Director in writing of the same within 30 days from the date of such conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely notify (even if due to unawareness) is a breach of the regulation; the Final Order notes Respondent did not inform OED until March 13, 2023 for a conviction occurring earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of suspended or excluded practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended or excluded practitioner must comply with the duties set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; Respondent provided a sworn declaration representing his compliance with § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a § 11.58 sworn declaration is a formal representation to OED and can be used to set suspension commencement nunc pro tunc; misrepresentation of compliance can trigger further discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction reflecting adversely on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A conviction of a crime that reflects adversely on the practitioner's fitness as a practitioner violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions may constitute unethical conduct warranting discipline if they bear on fitness to practice; the Final Order finds Respondent violated § 11.804(b) based on specified convictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office for twenty-four (24) months; the suspension shall commence nunc pro tunc on November 3, 2023 (date of § 11.58 sworn declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the agreed length and effective date of suspension as the disciplinary sanction for the misconduct; suspension may be extended under the Agreement's terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition: compliance with criminal Judgment and Sentencing Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order requires Respondent to comply with all conditions and obligations imposed in the Judgment and Sentencing documents entered in the underlying criminal case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with the criminal sentence conditions is a basis for further disciplinary action under the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for additional suspension (Order to Show Cause process)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director in good faith believes Respondent violated sentencing conditions, the Agreement authorizes issuance of an Order to Show Cause, sending it to Respondent's last address, granting 15 days to respond, and—if OED continues to believe there was noncompliance—delivering materials to the USPTO Director to request immediate suspension for up to an additional twenty-four (24) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the stepwise procedural protections and deadlines (issue, service, 15-day response, evidence and argument delivery to USPTO Director) before additional immediate suspension is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED may seek discrete discipline for underlying misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement prevents the OED Director from seeking discrete discipline for any misconduct that formed the basis for an Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED retains authority to pursue separate disciplinary counts or measures beyond invoking the Agreement's additional-suspension mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and USPTO electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's name shall be dissociated from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), and Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number or a USPTO verified Electronic System account unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical consequence of suspension: removal of electronic privileges and prohibition on re-obtaining accounts until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice of disciplinary action is required; Official Gazette text must be materially consistent with the Order's summary of facts and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records may be used to escalate future discipline or rebut mitigation claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to reconsideration, review, or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By agreement, the respondent gives up procedural appellate/review remedies; such waivers are explicit terms of settlement orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered (acknowledgement, contrition, cooperation, remediation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order notes that Respondent acknowledged ethical lapses, demonstrated genuine contrition, accepted responsibility, cooperated with OED's investigation (providing sua sponte supplemental responses), and completed remedial measures (12-week substance abuse program; over 50 hours of cognitive behavioral therapy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating facts were considered in reaching the agreed sanction; documentation of remediation and cooperation may reduce the severity of discipline in settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement allocates litigation/administrative costs to the parties rather than imposing costs or fines as part of the sanction.
